edges.description: Disrupted neural-lineage differentiation (the PAX6 decrease) is the proposed cellular route to the developmental delay documented in exposed children; the steps are not established.
Maternal dosing delivers carbamazepine to the embryo during organogenesis, the initiating step of the mechanism curated here.

edges.description: The assay reproduces the differentiation-disruption arm of the mechanism in human cells — carbamazepine lowers the cardiomyocyte (MYH6), hepatocyte (FOXA2, AFP) and neural-ectoderm (PAX6) markers concentration-dependently. It does not reproduce the syndrome's defining craniofacial dysmorphism or fingernail hypoplasia, and it carries no reactive-metabolite readout, so it speaks to the cellular differentiation effect only.
edges.limitations: A 2D hiPSC differentiation reads gene-expression biomarkers of three lineages, not craniofacial morphogenesis or nail development; its metabolic competence for forming the arene-oxide intermediates is not characterized, so the proposed proximate teratogen may be under-represented.

nodes.description: Delay in early development, the neurodevelopmental component of the syndrome.

nodes.description: Carbamazepine is oxidized to carbamazepine-10,11-epoxide and, by oxidation on the aromatic ring, to arene-oxide and quinone intermediates. These reactive species, rather than the parent drug, are the proposed teratogens; their normal clearance is by epoxide hydrolase, so reduced detoxification capacity is thought to raise susceptibility. In the mouse, the epoxide metabolite is itself teratogenic at exposures achievable in vivo.
nodes.id: Formation of Reactive Arene Oxide Metabolites

evidence.reference_title: Teratogenicity of carbamazepine-10, 11-epoxide and oxcarbazepine in the SWV mouse.
evidence.snippet: These data are consistent with a teratogenic CBZ metabolite, possibly CBZE, or with oxidation of CBZE or CBZ at positions on the aromatic ring leading to the formation of reactive intermediates such as arene oxides or quinones.

evidence.reference_title: Teratogenicity of antiepileptic drugs: role of drug metabolism and pharmacogenomics.
evidence.snippet: systems such as epoxide hydrolase, glutathione reductase, superoxide dismutase and other toxin-scavenging systems may be important modifiers that lower the risk

nodes.description: Carbamazepine exposure lowers the differentiation of multiple embryonic lineages. In the ReproTracker human iPSC assay it reduces the cardiomyocyte marker MYH6, the endoderm/hepatocyte markers FOXA2 and AFP, and the neural-ectoderm marker PAX6 in a concentration-dependent manner — a broader lineage effect than thalidomide's in the same assay, which spared the neural lineage.

evidence.reference_title: Animal-free assessment of developmental toxicity: Combining PBPK modeling with the ReproTracker assay.
evidence.snippet: Exposure to carbamazepine led to a significant and concentration-dependent decrease in expression of the cardiomyocyte-specific marker (MYH6), liver-specific markers (FOXA2, and AFP), and neural ectoderm biomarker gene (PAX6), when compared to controls

nodes.description: Carbamazepine, taken for epilepsy, trigeminal neuralgia or bipolar disorder, reaching the embryo by placental transfer. It is the necessary cause of the syndrome. Carbamazepine is extensively oxidized in the liver, and one of its principal routes generates carbamazepine-10,11-epoxide and other reactive arene-oxide intermediates, which is the basis of the reactive-metabolite mechanism below.

evidence.reference_title: Pattern of malformations in the children of women treated with carbamazepine during pregnancy.
evidence.snippet: That carbamazepine itself is teratogenic is indicated by the incidence of craniofacial defects (11 percent), fingernail hypoplasia (26 percent), and developmental delay (20 percent) in the 35 live-born children of the women in the prospective study who were exposed prenatally to carbamazepine alone.

nodes.description: A human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC) biomarker assay in which cells are differentiated toward cardiomyocytes, hepatocytes and neural rosettes under compound exposure, with lineage- and cell-specific marker genes quantified. Carbamazepine classified as a teratogen in the assay, lowering markers across all three lineages. Used with a pregnancy PBPK model to derive human-equivalent doses; only the in vitro biomarker arm is linked to the pathograph.
Carbamazepine crosses the placenta and reaches the embryo during organogenesis. This node is the shared parent of the reactive-metabolite branch and the cell-differentiation readout below.
